Hi Alice / PayWise security team —

Thanks for the detailed questions. High-level answers here; attaching a more detailed implementation note (kms-implementation-notes.pdf) and happy to cover in the deep dive.

1) Customer-managed keys support
- Cloud KMS: Yes. We support AWS KMS (symmetric and asymmetric keys), GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. Customers can configure envelope encryption where Redwood holds data encryption keys (DEKs) and those DEKs are wrapped by customer-managed KEKs in their KMS.
- BYOK/HSM: For Private deployments and on-prem installs we support integration with customer HSMs and FIPS 140-2/3-backed modules. We also support Bring-Your-Own-Key material (imported keys) where allowed by the cloud vendor.

2) Key rotation and backwards compatibility
- Rotation is supported via key versioning in the customer's KMS. Previously encrypted objects remain readable because we keep key-wrapping metadata and support lazy re-encryption or on-read rewrap depending on policy. No planned downtime for rotation.
- We recommend a staged rotation and can provide an automation script to rewrap DEKs if you want all data re-encrypted proactively.

3) Audit logging
- We emit request-level audit logs that include key id, caller identity (service principal), operation (Encrypt/Decrypt), timestamp, and region. Logs can be exported to your logging endpoint (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Log Analytics) or pushed to a SIEM via syslog/forwarder. Retention configurable per your logging pipeline; Redwood can retain 90 days by default and deliver longer-term copies on request.

4) Data retention controls
- Our platform supports per-route and per-model retention policies; you can attach retention TTLs to stored artifacts and chat history. For longer legal holds (e.g., 7 years) we recommend pairing retention policies with export/archival features (S3/GCS buckets under your control).

Other notes
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; mTLS available for Private deployments.
- At-rest: AES-256 envelope encryption for data at rest. Root key (KEK) lifecycle is controlled in customer-managed KMS when configured.
- Key destruction: If you require cryptographic proof-of-destruction, we can outline a process for key material deletion and for sealed key removal from our control plane; for BYOK in HSMs, destruction is controlled by you.
- SLA/operational impact: Using external KMS adds latency to initialization/decryption operations (usually single-digit ms extra per key unwrap); we can benchmark this on your workload during the deep dive.
